summary: Checkpointing is not what causes the ~26 s gap in T03 requests 2 and 3. When a later call only reads `raw`, the checkpointers add 0.10-0.15 s, because sizes are reused by address and fingerprint. With checkpointing off, those calls change by no more than 0.15 s; the gap comes from risk and gate sizing, which other agents are covering. The large checkpoint cost falls on calls that create or rebind a big object. After such a call, env_snapshot re-sizes the binding with env_snap_size(), and 85-89% of that time is unique.default() over every character column plus a global unique(unlist()). Measured locally: checkpoint_after median 5.65 s (range 4.69-6.93) for a T03-sized list (1,231 data.tables, which gptr sizes at 4.5e9 B), 1.66 s at 250 tables and 0.91 s at 125. Each such sizing also allocates an extra +3.4-3.5 GB of heap at 1,231 tables. This is the same mechanism as the benchmark's 13.9 s: in its own profile, env_snapshot takes 13.07 s of the 13.87 s checkpoint_after. A reassign of `raw` costs 3.98 s at 1,231 tables, and 2.05 s at 250 tables, where a by-reference image is also kept and walked a second time. In-place edits of objects over the undo budget cost about 5 ms, but only when gptr may write images to disk (a `.gptr` folder or a human present). In that case a predicted in-place edit writes a full image before the call: 0.87-0.95 s and 705 MB per call for a 0.46 GB object. Many objects cost per call +0.17 s at 1,000 bindings and +2.1-2.3 s at 10,000; the first call at 10,000 costs +7.3 s, mostly env_snap_size walking the ~70-frame call stack once per binding. The after-loop is O(n²) (match() per binding: 2.84 s at 30,000). File scans are capped at 2,000 entries and cost about 0.3-0.45 ms per entry. In a T03-like project root (1,231 linked TSVs), they add 0.31-0.47 s inside the call and 0.31-0.45 s at request end, which matches the benchmark's ckpt_files_before of 0.52-0.92 s. With checkpointing off, checkpoint_before plus checkpoint_after fall to 1-5 ms, and the T03-sized create call drops from 13.3 s to 7.2 s. Contention: load average was 8-14 on 16 cores during the runs, and N=1231 repetitions varied by up to about 20%. Memory: the N=1231 end-to-end processes peaked at 11.8-13.1 GiB RSS, above the ~12 GB target.

causes.title: Sizing a new or rebound large object in the after-snapshot (env_snap_size string de-duplication)
causes.where: R/ckpt-objects.R:547 (ck$snap = env_snapshot in ckpt_objects_after); R/env-snapshot.R:157-173 (size recomputed unless address/class/shape/fp match previous); R/utils-size.R:133-137 (unique.default(x) stored for every character vector), :66-69 (unique(unlist(mget(...)))), :43, :209 (second string pass when a list is sampled past env_size_budget = 10,000 parts)
causes.mechanism: After a call, env_snapshot sizes every binding whose address, class, shape or fingerprint changed. For a list of data.tables, env_snap_size walks about 714 tables before it starts sampling (10,000-part budget). For each table it hashes 3 character columns of 60,664 strings with unique.default and keeps the results. It then unlists and unique()s all of them, and runs a second pass over the sampled strings. That is about 86-127M string pointers hashed and a ~1 GB transient STRSXP. Walking the numeric data costs almost nothing.
causes.cost: Measured, create call (T03 request-1 analogue), checkpoint_after median: 5.65 s (4.69/5.65/6.93) at N=1231 (gptr size 4.50e9 B; object.size 1.51e10); 1.66 s at N=250; 0.91 s at N=125. Unit env_snap_size(raw) median: 5.03 s (1231), 2.30 s (500), 0.85 s (250), 0.55 s (125). Transient R heap per call: +3.39-3.51 GB at N=1231 (base 4.47 GB), +0.90-1.05 GB at N=250. Rprof: unique.default 85-89% self, unlist 8-13%. The benchmark (AWS) saw 13.87 s, with env_snapshot at 13.07 s.
causes.safety_role: Provides the bytes column used by the next call's capture plan (ref, disk or skip against gptr.undo_capture_max 1e8, undo_max_bytes 1e9 and undo_spill_max 2e9), the sizes in fragment rows and in the 'modified without an undo copy' notes, and the memory-budget accounting. Removing it loses size-based undo decisions and size text, not undo itself. A cheaper size estimate or a size cache shared with the risk path would keep the role.
causes.scales_with: Character vectors reached × their length (capped near 714 tables, then extrapolated), i.e. object size and structure. Paid once per new binding and again on every address or fingerprint change.

causes.title: Rebinding a large object: recompute plus unshared-bytes walk of the retained by-reference image
causes.where: R/ckpt-objects.R:411-420 (capture plan: an assign target up to 1e9 B gets 'ref'), :142-150 (ckpt_capture), :527 and :312-317 (ckpt_unshared_bytes = env_snap_size(image, shared = current))
causes.mechanism: A predicted assign (including the dead `if (!exists('raw')) raw = ...` branch) of an object up to 1 GB keeps the old value by reference. If the address changes, the after-snapshot re-sizes the new value, and ckpt_unshared_bytes walks the current value as `shared` and then the image: two more full string passes. Above 1 GB the plan is 'skip', and only the re-size happens.
causes.cost: Measured checkpoint_after for `raw = c(raw, list(note = 'x'))`: N=250 median 2.05 s (snapshot 0.96 + unshared 1.02); N=125 0.91 s (0.44 + 0.47); N=1231 3.98 s (snapshot only; over 1e9, so skip). The held image counts 184 unshared bytes, so its memory cost is small.
causes.safety_role: Allows undoing a rebinding of objects up to 1 GB without copying them; held-bytes accounting for the 1 GB in-memory budget.
causes.scales_with: Object size and structure (as C1), times 2-3 walks; only when the binding's address changes.

causes.title: Eager full disk image before a predicted in-place modify of a 100 MB-2 GB object (only when spill is allowed)
causes.where: R/ckpt-objects.R:416 (plan 'disk'), :476-482, :169-174 (ckpt_capture_disk), :160-164 (ckpt_write_image = serialize_leaf(xdr = FALSE) + write_atomic); :371-373 (spill allowed only with .gptr/ or a human present)
causes.mechanism: Before the call runs, the whole object is serialized into an in-memory raw vector and written atomically to <workspace>/checkpoints/objects/<sid>/<key>.rdsx. serialize writes every string element in full, so the file is about 1.5× gptr's de-duplicated size. This did not happen in the benchmark: it ran non-interactive with no .gptr/, so spill was off and objects over 100 MB were 'skip'.
causes.cost: Measured with .gptr/ at N=125 (gptr size 0.46 GB): checkpoint_before 0.87-0.95 s per predicted-modify call, 705,285,432 B written per call (1.41 GB on disk after 2 calls), RSS 1.67 → 3.05 GB. Unit at N=250: serialize 1.31 s for 1.41 GB, ckpt_write_image median 3.38 s (1.76-3.73), heap +1.35 GB. Rprof: serialize 43%, writeBin 2-3% of the call.
causes.safety_role: Restorable undo of an in-place edit to a large object (copy-on-modify does not apply to edits R makes in place).
causes.scales_with: Serialized object size; per predicted-modify call, before execution; not done above gptr.undo_spill_max (2e9).

causes.title: Per-binding snapshot, capture and settle work with many objects (settle is O(n²))
causes.where: R/env-snapshot.R:136-176 (loop: tryCatch, env_snap_leaf at :82-88 → env_shape/env_fmt_n format(), fingerprint SHA-256); R/ckpt-objects.R:142-150 (id_new SHA-256 and assign per ref capture), :426-451 (gptr_preimage S3 dispatch per binding), :500-538 and :555-558 (ckpt_settle_row per binding: data.frame row subset plus match(nm, post$name) at :505)
causes.mechanism: Every value binding is snapshotted twice per call (before and after), offered to gptr_preimage, captured by reference with a fresh SHA-256 key, then settled row by row. The per-row match() over all post names makes the after loop quadratic.
causes.cost: Measured end-to-end, warm call: +0.17 s at 1,000 bindings (before 0.083, after 0.093) and +2.1-2.3 s at 10,000 (before 0.83-0.92, after 1.23-1.28; on 3.17-3.47 s vs off 1.04-1.34 s). Unit (objects checkpointer alone), before/after: 0.16/0.10 s (1k), 0.24/0.28 (3k), 0.80/1.30 (10k), 2.76/8.13 (30k). Micro: match loop 0.32 s (10k), 2.84 s (30k); row subset 0.23 s (10k), 0.69 s (30k). Rprof, warm 10k call: env_snap_facts 64% (env_shape/format 39%, fingerprint 14%), ckpt_settle_row 19%, ckpt_capture 6.6%. Pure reads skip all of this (5 ms).
causes.safety_role: Detects changes (address plus fingerprint) and keeps a copy-free by-reference undo image of every value binding until the call settles; unchanged images are released.
causes.scales_with: Number of bindings: before is linear; after is quadratic (match).

causes.title: First checkpointed call sizes every binding cold; each env_snap_size walks the whole call stack
causes.where: R/utils-size.R:24-33 (every frame on the stack and its enclosure chain marked seen: env_size_top/identical/topenv/assign); called once per binding from R/env-snapshot.R:171 while ck$snap is NULL (R/ckpt-objects.R:464)
causes.mechanism: With no previous snapshot, every binding is sized. Each env_snap_size call first walks all ~70 frames of the served-call stack (peter → reactor → hooks → mcp dispatch → checkpointer) and their enclosures, so the per-object cost is dominated by stack depth rather than object size.
causes.cost: Measured: first call with 10,000 small objects, checkpoint_before 7.3 s (7.32 median; outer 10.26 s on vs 1.74 s off), against env_snapshot cold 1.02 s in a shallow unit call. Rprof: env_size_top 34%, identical 22%, assign 13% of the call; stack depth 68-72 frames. With 1,000 objects: +0.75 s.
causes.safety_role: Keeps frames of running calls (and a function-frame home) out of sizes.
causes.scales_with: Bindings × stack depth; once per session, plus once per new binding later.

causes.title: Files checkpointer: bounded project scans before the call, after the call and at turn end
causes.where: R/ckpt-files.R:444-466 (before: sync scan, once per turn in per-turn mode, :447), :508-529 (after: scan unless per-turn; switch at :517 when walk_secs > gptr.checkpoint_scan_budget 0.25 s), :537-545 and R/ckpt-rewind.R:237-255 (turn-end scan in agent_end); R/ckpt-scan.R:27-220 (≤2,000 entries ckpt_entry_max :12, ≤256 captures :144, ≤1e8 bytes, 2 s timeout); skipped for file-free calls (R/ckpt-rewind.R:46-49)
causes.mechanism: Each scan stats every entry up to 2,000 (path_info, Sys.readlink, ps_fs_stat, file.access, path_class) and hashes with xxh128, and touches the blob of, up to 256 capturable files: ≤1 MB each at baseline, ≤50 MB later. New contents are copied into the blob store (gzip level 1 up to 8 MB). Once a scan takes over 0.25 s or stops early, the session switches to one sync per turn plus one turn-end scan.
causes.cost: Measured end-to-end. 1,000 files: first call 2.08 s on vs 0.82 s off (before 0.75, after 0.48); first call of turn 2 0.43 vs 0.04 s; turn-end scan 0.39-0.46 s per request. 20,000 files: first call before 0.96 s (stops at 2,000 entries, partial coverage), turn 2 +0.55 s, turn-end 0.52-0.72 s. T03-like root (1,231 TSVs linked to one 4.2 MB file): +0.31-0.47 s per request in the call (sym: request 2 0.80 vs 0.31 s, request 3 0.36 vs 0.03 s) plus 0.31-0.45 s at agent_end, which matches the benchmark's ckpt_files_before 0.52-0.92 s. About 0.3-0.45 ms per entry. Rprof: path_class 34-43%, ckpt_is_link 10-22%, ckpt_regular 11-18%, ckpt_store_put 6-16%.
causes.safety_role: File undo/rewind from content-addressed blobs, including writes the code analysis did not predict; created/modified/deleted reports and coverage notices.
causes.scales_with: min(project entries, 2,000), plus the count and size of capturable files; independent of what the call writes. Per turn rather than per call once a scan is slow.

causes.title: Copy-safety cost: by-reference pre-images force duplicates on the agent's next in-place edit and stay in memory
causes.where: R/ckpt-objects.R:142-150 (ref capture), :180-193 (settle keeps changed images), :731-745 (turn-end budget: drop after gptr.undo_turns 20, spill or drop above gptr.undo_max_bytes 1e9)
causes.mechanism: Holding a reference raises the refcount, so `x[1] = 0` on a captured value of 100 MB or less copies the whole vector. The old value is kept as the undo image until the budget drops or spills it at agent_end.
causes.cost: Measured with 12 numeric vectors of 90 MB, 3 modified per request. R time 0.024-0.036 s vs 0.007-0.011 s off (+17-29 ms per 270 MB). Held images grew 0.27 → 1.08 GB, then were capped at 0.99 GB by the budget. Peak RSS 2.59-2.60 GiB on vs 1.50 GiB off. With .gptr/, agent_end spilled 1-3 images in 0.045-0.13 s, 360 MB on disk.
causes.safety_role: Exact undo of in-place edits to objects up to 100 MB without copying anything at capture time.
causes.scales_with: Size of modified captured values; retained memory is capped at undo_max_bytes per session.

causes.title: Fixed per-call overhead: repeated code parsing, state snapshot, session entry
causes.where: R/ckpt-rewind.R:37-41 and :55-61 (ckpt_pure_read → ckpt_predict once per checkpointer for level-0 code); R/ckpt-objects.R:386-394 and :467; R/ckpt-files.R:395-400 (ckpt_call_paths parses again); R/ckpt-objects.R:805-845 (state: options(), Sys.getenv(), search(), connections, RNG hash); R/agent-dispatch.R:387-404 (run_append_custom)
causes.mechanism: code_targets() parses the same code 2-5 times per call; the state checkpointer copies the options and environment-variable lists twice; one gptr.checkpoint entry is appended to the session JSONL.
causes.cost: Measured: ckpt_predict about 10-17 ms per parse of the 25-line T03 code (0.035 s for 2 parses in create); state before plus after 1-22 ms; run_append_custom 1-2 ms. Checkpointed small call total about 0.01-0.06 s; pure read 5-6 ms. Session file grows 0.42-0.46 KB per objects-only call and 0.9-1.3 KB per call with file rows (11-call run: 15.3 KB off vs 20.0 KB on).
causes.safety_role: Pure-read detection (skips all checkpointers); undo of options, working directory and attached packages; the durable fragment record used by /undo, /rewind and gptr_checkpoints().

causes.title: checkpoint.note re-snapshots the whole workspace without a previous snapshot for each permission question
causes.where: R/ckpt-objects.R:751-780 (env_snapshot(envir) at :761 with no `previous`), called from R/agent-dispatch.R:788-789 (perm_request_record) and R/console-ui.R:364-370
causes.mechanism: Every permission question with an undo note sizes every binding from scratch (C1 plus C5 cost), separately from ck$snap.
causes.cost: Not measured directly (no question is asked in auto mode). By construction it equals a cold env_snapshot: measured 5.41 s (N=1231 unit), 0.89 s (N=250), 1.02 s for 10k objects in a shallow stack (7 s+ in the served stack).
causes.safety_role: The 'cannot be undone: ...' line in permission prompts.
causes.scales_with: Workspace size and binding count, once per permission question.

causes.title: Same object sized again outside the checkpointer (context, not checkpoint cost)
causes.where: R/env-snapshot.R:485-490 and :388-404 (P09 workspace memory: env_on_agent_end / workspace_changes keep their own previous snapshot); risk_binding_info (R/perm-classify.R ~2298) in the pre-gate and gate
causes.mechanism: ck$snap, P09's mem$snapshot and the risk classifier each compute env_snap_size(raw) on their own; nothing shares a size cache keyed on address and fingerprint.
causes.cost: Measured at N=1231: the P09 request-end re-size of raw is 4.43-5.97 s in request 1 and 3.87-4.72 s after the reassign, outside the tool interval and still present with checkpoint off (5.92 s). Risk pre-gate 4.2-5.2 s and gate 4.4-5.3 s per later call (other agents' scope).
causes.safety_role: Workspace change block for the model, and risk notes.
causes.scales_with: Object size and structure, per request (P09) and per call (risk).

open_questions: The benchmark (AWS) is about 2.4× slower than this machine for the same step (13.07 s vs 5.5 s env_snapshot). It is unclear how much comes from CPU speed and how much from real TCGA strings, which are longer than my synthetic IDs.
The benchmark's ckpt_objects_before of 0.89 s in request 2 was not reproduced (0.02-0.03 s here). It may be a GC pause attributed to that frame with a 5 GB heap.

The Codex CLI route was not reproduced: the fake provider is not type 'cli', so ckpt_on_cli's agent_start sync and turn_end scan, and sync = FALSE for served calls, did not run. In the real benchmark those scans fall into harness time between tool calls.
ckpt_note (checkpoint.note in permission prompts) was not measured directly; its cost is inferred from cold env_snapshot timings.
The benchmark README says a default-checkpoint gptr_doc replay 'exceeded the memory guard'. This fits the measured +3.4-3.5 GB transient per env_snap_size of raw, but the doc path was not measured.
Machine contention: load average was 8-14 on 16 cores during the runs; N=1231 repetitions varied by up to ±20%.
N=1231 end-to-end processes peaked at 11.8-13.1 GiB RSS, slightly over the ~12 GB target; no further N=1231 runs were made.
